Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of advice/social context including healthy adult participants (18–45) and reports neural effects of advice; however the reported whole-brain analyses focus on developmental (between-group) contrasts and age-related linear effects rather than presenting an unmasked, whole-brain, within-group task activation map for the healthy adult group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (contains a healthy adult group). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level, task-evoked statistical map identified as coming specifically from the healthy adult group that is generalizable to adults). Therefore Exclusion criterion E4 applies (reports only between-group/interaction contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). fulltext_incomplete=false

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 25–49) that investigates social-related processing (emotion sharing, empathy, interpersonal understanding) using task-based fMRI while participants viewed emotionally-laden movie clips. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (intersubject correlation maps and GLMs relating valence/arousal to ISC) with voxelwise permutation testing and FDR correction, presented in figures and supplementary tables. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it reports task-based fMRI during a social-affective task (the Socio-affective Video Task; compassion generation/response to others’ distress) (I3); the sample consists of healthy adult participants (female, ages 18–35) with results reported for the healthy group (I4); the paper presents group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked results (HE vs LE contrasts, parametric modulations) with FWE-corrected maps and coordinate tables (I5); results are reported in text, figures, and supplementary materials (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-group healthy task effects). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study that explicitly investigates simulation of others' decisions — a social-cognition task (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (36 analyzed; ages reported as adults; meets I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain univariate analyses with family-wise-error cluster correction (p<0.05), peak coordinates, and tables of activated clusters for task regressors (sRPE, sAPE, decision variables), i.e., healthy-group whole-brain task effects (meets I5 and I6). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Figures, Tables, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper). Therefore this study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment that directly probes social-motivational processing (affiliation vs. power) using film clips, satisfying the review’s social-related constructs. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=17 males, mean age 23.6), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task contrasts (affiliation>control; power>control) and regression analyses linking these contrasts to motive scores, with reported clusters and MNI coordinates and mixed-effects inference—fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. Full article text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range age) are met. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social-intention understanding in healthy adults. It uses task-based functional MRI during observation of social interactions (social-related constructs: perception/understanding of others), with 27 healthy adult participants (ages within 17–65). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and provides thresholded statistical maps and tables of coordinates (FWE-corrected and uncorrected results) for contrasts (cooperative vs affective vs landscape), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy control sample are reported directly (no exclusive ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only results). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials are referenced but not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=19, ages 21–34) using a naturalistic social-perception task (viewing rated movie clips) and reporting group-level, whole-brain univariate GLM results (e.g., contrasts of social vs. non-social features; feature-specific t-maps; coordinates and thresholding p<0.05 FDR). Methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. The healthy adult sample, the task (social communication/perception), and univariate whole-brain maps meet inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of affiliative social processing in healthy adults (n=27, ages within 17–65). The task involved imagining social scenarios designed to evoke affiliative vs nonaffiliative conditions; behavioral and imaging methods are described in full. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses are reported, with voxel-level FWE-corrected results and coordinates (tables and figures) for affiliative versus nonaffiliative and valence contrasts. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social/attachment processing: mothers listened to infant cry (a social/attachment-related task) during functional MRI and results relate to attachment behaviors. Participants are healthy adults (primiparous mothers, mean age 24.1; screened with SCID and no participants met criteria for current major depressive episode at time of scanning), satisfying the healthy adult group requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (FSL/FLAME), with thresholding and cluster coordinates presented (Table 1, figures), and describes task-evoked maps for the healthy group. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of empathy/perspective-taking (social cognition) using healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 21–31). The methods describe whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (first- and second-level SPM analyses), with cluster- and peak-level FWE-corrected results and coordinates reported in tables/figures (e.g., Self vs Other, View-Pain vs View-No-Pain contrasts, conjunction analyses). The study therefore satisfies the review scope and reports whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps in standard coordinate tables and figures. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary figures, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes social reasoning tasks (theory of mind / emotion understanding) presented as texts and videos. Sample: 45 healthy adult participants (mean age 20.5, range 19–23), satisfying the healthy adult age criterion. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (GLM, random-effects analyses, multiple comparison correction) with peak coordinates provided (Appendix A) and figures showing task > rest and domain contrasts; results are generalizable to the healthy population. The paper is not ROI-only, not resting-only, and reports univariate group-level whole-brain activation maps for the healthy group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendices) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (perception of emotional facial expressions) with healthy adult human participants (N=23, ages 24–34). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses in humans with cluster-wise correction and presents whole-brain significance maps and stereotactic coordinates. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate results), and I6 (acceptable reporting via maps/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (action observation, mirror-neuron and mentalizing systems) in a sample of healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–32), satisfying the sample criterion. Analyses are group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts and the manuscript explicitly states that whole-brain results and details about the mask are provided in the Supplemental Material; reporting of group-level statistical maps (cluster results/coordinates) is provided in the text/tables, satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion (I5) and allowing supplemental reporting (I6). The task is clearly social-related (mentalizing/understanding others), satisfying I3. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only restriction, no connectivity/rest-only focus, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 17–65 range, and this is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social cognitive processing (visual perspective taking) in healthy adult participants (mean age 22.4; n=16 after exclusions). The paper reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., Inconsistent Other > Consistent Other; Consistent Self > Consistent Other) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction, and tables/figures of results. Healthy-group results are reported and generalizable to healthy adults. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining action observation and execution (mirror responses), which maps onto social cognitive processes (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample comprises 21 healthy adult participants (mean age 24), within the 17–65 range. The paper reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (mentions a whole-brain analysis at p<0.001 uncorrected and reports peak coordinates and clusters), in addition to ROI results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social cognition (contrast of interactive vs. observational social stimuli) using task-based BOLD in healthy adult participants (N=22; mean age 25). The methods describe group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (Three-Way repeated-measures whole-brain ANOVA) and report task-evoked effects; exploratory whole-brain results (e.g., early visual V1) are described in the text. ROI analyses/SVC were applied for hypothesis-driven tests, but whole-brain group-level testing was performed and reported. The sample falls within the 17–65 range and results are reported for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study that directly manipulates social information (trustworthiness judgments) during a task and reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and tables of peak coordinates. Sample consists of healthy adults (N analyzed=14, mean age 22) within the 17–65 range. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (empathy/perception of others’ pain), conducted in healthy adult participants (n≈36, ages ~21). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (painful vs non-painful stimuli) with FDR-corrected maps and tables of activations, and describes these results in the text (whole-brain analyses in pre- and post-priming sessions). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps generalizable to healthy adults), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of face gender perception, a form of social perception (Perception and Understanding of Others) using healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 19–42). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise random-effects analyses (contrast gender-different > gender-same) with reported clusters/coordinates and figures (right CoS, left precuneus, right lateral occipital gyrus, etc.). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level univariate voxelwise results), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (interpersonal resource conflict) in healthy adults (final N=17, mean age 23.5) that reports group-level whole-brain univariate activation contrasts (e.g., Conflict > No Conflict, interaction Human×Conflict) with thresholding and tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates neural correlates of abstract vs. concrete mindsets using tasks that engage social cognition (Why-How task probes ‘why’ people perform actions, recruiting the mentalizing network). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during social-related tasks involving perception/understanding of others), I4 (healthy adult sample: 24 right-handed participants, ages 18–27), I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked analyses with one-sample t-tests and voxelwise thresholds; conjunction analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text, tables, and figures). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not limited to connectivity-only or between-group-only contrasts, participants are within age range, and the paper contains original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Appendices).

This full-text reports an fMRI study of social perception (comparisons of physical attractiveness of other people), meeting the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social-related: beauty comparisons of other persons), I4 (sample: 25 healthy adult participants, mean age 23.46 within 17–65), I5 (group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts reported; voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds given), I6 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/tables and described in text). Full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and preprocessing), Results (whole-brain and ROI analyses with coordinates), and Discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore include for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using a social interaction task (modified cyberball) with healthy adult participants (N=15, ages ~24), meeting I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: univariate SPM group analyses (reported as null for the interaction) and an exploratory whole-brain searchlight (voxelwise random-effects group analysis) with corrected significant clusters (coordinates and t-values reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise reporting (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals) in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=25, ages 19–27; Experiment 2: n=14, ages 18–23), satisfying sample criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical) with voxel-wise thresholds, ROI extent thresholds, and tables/figures of results, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (scanned group N=38, ages 19–31) using a social task (real-world speed-dating) that probes affiliation/attachment and perception of others. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts and statistical maps (main effects and contrasts such as Yes > No, Match > Unrequited, violations of expectation) with tables of coordinates and thresholding details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not a between-group-only comparison, age range within 17–65, not a non-empirical paper). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This fMRI study investigates social communication (communicative vs private intentions) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=23, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt, interaction effects) with stereotaxic coordinates, thresholds, and tables/figures, and additionally reports PPI connectivity. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate results), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (handholding/social regulation of threat) in a healthy adult sample (N=22; mean age 23.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-wise tests using FSL/FLAME with Z>2.3, p<.05), and presents ROI/coordinate results in Table 1 and figures. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample 17–65; I5: group-level whole-brain univariate task-evoked results reported; I6: whole-brain results reported in table/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (laughter perception) in healthy adults (n=18, mean age 26), meeting the population criterion. The task explicitly probes social-related processing (laughter type categorization versus bout counting), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., CSL>TIC, TIC>CSL, CAT>COU) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinates/tables/figures, meeting whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 17–65, empirical data present). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (imitation of communicative gestures), meeting the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adults (20 analyzed; mean age 24.6), satisfying the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts (e.g., IMI>CT, S>NS) with voxel coordinates and cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo), and presents results across whole-brain contrasts in tables and figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This empirical fMRI study examines neural responses to others’ suffering (social cognition/empathy) in healthy adult participants (aged 18–45) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank interaction; whole-brain corrected results identifying IPC and DLPFC), along with ROI/PPI follow-ups. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps/results), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26) using a gambling task where participants played for self, best friend, and an antagonist. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (within-subject ANOVAs) with voxelwise results, tables of coordinates, figures, and whole-brain Person × Outcome interaction and main effects (with small-volume correction reported where applicable). All core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (interns N=19, mean age 20.55; producers N=79, mean age 20.54) examining social communication/mentalizing processes during a task in which participants considered recommending ideas (social-related task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects univariate analyses and reports voxelwise results and coordinates (thresholded whole-brain maps reported; Table 1, figures). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3: social fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample within 17–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating recognition of ‘vitality forms’ (social perception of others’ actions), using a task-based paradigm in healthy adults (N=19, ages 21–29). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (e.g., how vs what contrast) with voxelwise/cluster-level PFWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates. All required components (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the full text. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps generalizable to healthy adults), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition/theory-of-mind in healthy adults (N=46 females, age 18–31). The task probes perception/understanding of others (beliefs, emotions, pain), satisfying the social-related construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., B > Ph, E > Ph, Pa > Ph) with cluster-level inference using SnPM, and presents whole-brain maps and tables, meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no restricted age group, etc.). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (peer social-evaluation task) in a sample of healthy participants that includes adult participants (ages up to 22.9). It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (random-effects analyses) identifying MPFC activations and peak coordinates, and describes PPI connectivity results; whole-brain results are reported and corrected for multiple comparisons. The sample is healthy and contains an adult subgroup within the 17–65 range; although analyses model age continuously across childhood, adolescence, and young adulthood, the reported whole-brain maps derive from the healthy participant group and findings are discussed with respect to adult (young adult) outcomes. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

The article reports an fMRI task examining perception/understanding of others (nonverbal dyadic social interactions), using a behavioral rating during scanning (social-related task). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (21 males, ages 23–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (multiple contrasts, cluster-level corrected, with tables/coordinates and anatomical localization). Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression formation (perception/understanding of others) using BOLD fMRI during an explicit social task. Participants are healthy adults (N=19, mean age 19.1). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task contrasts and provides whole-brain coordinates and cluster-corrected results for the functional localizer (form-impression > sequencing) and main task (2×2 ANOVA), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception using passive viewing of biological (point-light) motion versus scrambled motion — a social-related task. It includes a healthy adult group (n=48, ages 20–35) reported separately, meeting the adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise contrasts (biological > scrambled) and Sex×Condition ANOVAs with cluster-corrected thresholds, tables, and figures describing healthy adult activation maps, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (complete). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-signal processing in healthy adults (ages 19–28) using tasks involving eye-gaze and self-propelling motion and an implicit mental-inference role-play. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., E–O and S–X; [E–O]+[S–X]) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and provides activation tables and figures. Sample meets the healthy adult age range and results for the healthy group are reported separately. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (third-party punishment/mentalizing), with healthy adult participants (N=26, mean age 26 within 17–65). The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain univariate analyses (GLM) with thresholding (q(FDR)<0.05) and lists Talairach coordinates and figures for activations (e.g., right TPJ, right anterior insula), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, empirical).

The study reports an fMRI task involving social cognition (viewing traffic campaign videos eliciting mentalizing/empathy), with healthy adult participants (male, ages 19–30) and group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (CV vs NV) reported for the healthy groups (within-group maps and figures). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

The study uses task-based fMRI of face perception (a social-related process) and includes a healthy adult sample (ages 18–37), satisfying I3 and I4. This fMRI study investigates attribute framing in social self-evaluation (perception/understanding of self), using task-based functional MRI in healthy adults (ages 19–41). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts are reported (e.g., positive vs negative frame; frame-inconsistent vs frame-consistent), with coordinates and cluster thresholds described, satisfying the requirement for univariate whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy sample. The study reports an fMRI experiment examining approachability judgments of faces (a social cognition task), clearly meeting I3. This paper reports task-based fMRI of a social-emotional paradigm (empathic judgments / emotional egocentricity bias), meeting the review objective. This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic social gestures) in healthy young adults. The full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=32, age range 18–39) performing a social-related task manipulating collaboration and competition while producing effort. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that probes social cognition: participants (n=20, ages 23–39, healthy) received tactile priming and made judgments about ambiguous social interactions (social coordination). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (ANOVA and post-hoc t-tests) with voxelwise results corrected for multiple comparisons (FDR), figures and tables of activation maps and coordinates (SI, SII, IFG, hippocampus, amygdala, etc.). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample in age range), I5 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported and generalized to healthy adults), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This paper reports voxel-based morphometry (structural MRI) analyses linking grey-matter volume to proneness to moral sentiments in healthy adults (N=63). It does not present task-evoked fMRI whole-brain, group-level univariate activation maps from healthy participants. Although a previously collected SSC-BOLD response from a subgroup (N=29) was used as a predictor in secondary analyses, the article does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps or primary fMRI task results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (study uses functional MRI during a social-related task in the reported analyses) and I5 (reports at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). It meets I4 (healthy adult sample reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly triggered by this manuscript.

This is an empirical fMRI study of live verbal social interaction (social communication) using simultaneous scanning of pairs. Participants were healthy adults (22 right-handed women, mean age 27.2), satisfying the sample age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise second-level t-tests (design-based analyses for talking, listening, imagining) with cluster-corrected thresholds, presented in text, figures, and supplementary tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social evaluation (trustworthiness and attractiveness) using explicit social-judgment tasks on vocal stimuli (meets I3). The sample comprises 44 healthy right-handed adults aged 21–60 (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (first- and second-level GLM), cluster-level FWE-corrected results, MNI coordinates, tables and figures (meets I5 and I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/empathy in healthy adults (n=27, mean age 34), using task-based fMRI with naturalistic video stimuli assessing social/empathic processing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts, conjunction analyses, MNI coordinates, and figures of activations (i.e., univariate voxelwise task-evoked maps) for the healthy participant group. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social cognition (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation), in a sample of healthy adults (15 right-handed males, ages 18–40). This paper reports task-based fMRI during social-related processing (familiar vs unfamiliar faces; affiliation/attachment/social cognition), includes a healthy control group of older adult participants with reported group-level within-group contrasts, and provides whole-brain, voxelwise group activation results (partner>unfamiliar) for the control group with FWE-corrected maps and coordinates. The study therefore meets criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult control group), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate task-evoked maps from controls), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Confidence moderate-high due to clear reporting of healthy-group whole-brain activations; age of control group is reported as mean 64.5 (SD 5.7) which is within the adult range but near the upper bound, but not documented as exclusively outside 17–65, so I4 is considered satisfied.

This empirical fMRI study uses a social task (ultimatum game) and includes a healthy adult group (ages 19–28). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (unfair–fair offers) and one-sample t-tests for each group, with thresholded statistical maps and tables of activations referenced for the healthy adult group. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 19–28), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate maps reported for healthy adults), and I6 (results reported as maps/tables described in text). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (free online imitation) in healthy adults. Sample: 23 right-handed healthy female adults aged 18–30 (meets age/sample criterion). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate GLM results (contrasts: imitating, being imitated, observation vs rest) with multiple-comparison correction (FWE p<0.05) and provides activation coordinates/tables and figures (Table 1, Fig. 3). Although PPI connectivity analyses are reported, the study also provides task-evoked whole-brain activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used natural interpersonal touch (social-related task) in healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 met). However, the paper does not report a group-level univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (e.g., GLM main-effect or within-group voxelwise contrast). Instead, results are based on group ICA spatial components and component time courses (multivariate decomposition). Per the review criteria, studies that report only ICA/connectivity-type analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map are excluded (E3). Therefore I5 (whole-brain univariate group map) is not met, and the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants (undergraduate sample, mean age ~18.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8 second-level GLM) with significant clusters and tables/figures (bilateral fusiform gyrus activations; suprathreshold voxel counts recorded; group activations shown at corrected thresholds). Results for the healthy/control group are reported and generalizable to healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI including social-distance trials (names/photos of friends vs acquaintances), satisfying the social-related processing requirement. Participants are healthy adults (N=15; ages 20–28), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (paired t tests and conjunctions across within-domain contrasts); although these univariate tests yielded no significant clusters at FDR-corrected thresholds, the analyses and results are reported at the group whole-brain level (text and tables/figures for MVPA and univariate results), satisfying the whole-brain reporting criterion. Reporting formats meet acceptable forms. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study includes healthy adult participants and uses task-based fMRI of social processing (I3 and I4 satisfied). Therefore exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies, and inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-evaluative task (direct, reflected, and other evaluations across social/academic/physical domains), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes adults in required age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (bystander effect) using an unrelated color-naming task while participants viewed emergency scenes, which is a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others; action preparation to help). Sample: healthy adults (N=17, ages 18–27; one excluded for technical failure but group-level results reported), within 17–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate voxelwise analyses (parametric GLM, contrasts, cluster-level corrections) with results described and tables/figures of clusters and statistical thresholds. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social (causal attribution/mentalizing) processing in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–41). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., self>truth, other>truth, conjunction) with whole-brain results and FWE-corrected peaks and coordinate tables. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The paper reports an fMRI experiment using a social attribution task (attributing awareness to a cartoon, i.e., social-related processing) in healthy adult participants (N=50, ages 18–49). This is an fMRI study of social processing (Cyberball exclusion and subsequent social decision-making) reporting task-evoked, group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (multiple whole-brain contrasts and tables of coordinates are reported). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (not truncated).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (anticipatory interpersonal touch) in healthy adults. Sample: 16 healthy right-handed adults, ages 20–34 (meets age/sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, voxel-wise whole-brain random-effects analyses and corrected cluster-level inference with coordinates, figures, and tables (meets whole-brain evidence criterion). This is an fMRI study of self- and other-referential episodic recollection (social cognition/self-understanding), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 19–29). The study uses task-based fMRI to examine facial color processing, which is clearly framed as social-information processing (perception/understanding of others and social communication). This is an empirical fMRI study of social feedback processing (a social-related task assessing self/other trait evaluation and conformity). This fMRI study investigates social influence/emotional alignment in interactive one-to-one social communication, using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age ~24). The article reports an fMRI study using a social-related task (first-person video clips of reactive-aggressive, social-positive, and neutral interactions) with a healthy adult sample (n=20 males, mean age 24.6). This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=19, mean age 26.5) using a social-related task (imagining triadic social interactions vs. self/other/iron control), reporting group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., triad>iron, conjunctions) with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activations and PPI analyses. This is an fMRI study of socially relevant processing (reaction to opponents' angry vs. neutral facial expressions during an interactive Taylor Aggression Paradigm) in healthy adult participants (32 males, mean age 23.3). Results are presented for the healthy sample and are generalizable to healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study that directly investigates social attribution (why/how task comparing social vs nonsocial stimuli), uses healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 21–46), and reports group-level whole-brain univariate analyses (why>how contrasts, conjunctions, cluster-corrected t-statistic maps; ROI analyses supplement but whole-brain results are clearly reported). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study employed task-based fMRI (SAMT) probing social-affective modulation of mimicry (affiliation/other-related processing). Participants were healthy adults (final N=41; mean age 22.6, range within 17–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (Incongruent>Congruent and masked interaction contrasts) with cluster-level whole-brain correction and tables of peak coordinates, and describes univariate whole-brain statistical maps and ROI-independent correlation analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results (behavioral and fMRI), and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (social incentive delay task with social reward) in healthy adults (fMRI cohort N=63; ages 20.4–36.6). The paper reports group-level, univariate task-evoked whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected results and tables/figures for anticipation and outcome contrasts across the healthy cohort) rather than only ROI or connectivity results. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material is noted but not required. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (social working memory and perspective-taking). It reports data from 25 healthy adult participants (mean age 21.56), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper includes group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise univariate analyses (conjunction and contrast parametric modulation analyses) with voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction and tables/figures of significant clusters/coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of gaze following (social attention/communication) in healthy adult participants (N=21, mean age 24.6). The task is clearly social (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (multiple main effects and specific contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. All required methodological details (participants, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM, contrasts, group random-effects) and whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 17–65, empirical original data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

The study uses fMRI of multiple social-related tasks in a healthy adult sample (I3 and I4 satisfied) and reports peak coordinates/figures (I6 satisfied). However, although whole-brain GLMs were run at the single-subject level, the reported group-level statistical analyses and maps were explicitly restricted to a bilateral STS mask (second-level analyses restricted to STS). The paper therefore does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map generalizable to healthy adults. This constitutes reporting results within a region-of-interest mask rather than whole-brain group maps, meeting exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map reported). Hence excluded under E2.

This is an fMRI study directly examining how people conceptualize actions at different levels of abstraction, recruiting healthy adult participants (N=17; age range 21–46). The task probes social-cognitive constructs (mentalizing/theory-of-mind, understanding others’ actions) and uses BOLD fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Why>How, LOA parametric effects) with cluster-level FWE correction and supplementary tables/figures, clearly attributable to the healthy control group. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=30, mean age 24.2) that uses face perception tasks (gender identification of angry and happy faces) which are social-related processes (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (FWE-corrected whole-brain and ROI analyses are described for main effects and interactions), with results clearly attributed to the healthy sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range age) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social/mentalizing task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) in a sample of 164 healthy subjects and describes activation of the mentalizing network and correlations with attachment dimensions, indicating group-level task-evoked whole-brain results. These satisfy inclusion criteria: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked activations reported), and I6 (results described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) appear to apply. However, the provided full text appears incomplete (only highlights/abstract and metadata are shown) and does not explicitly report participant ages or full methods in the supplied content; therefore I set fulltext_incomplete=true and assign moderate confidence.

The study uses task-based fMRI to investigate spontaneous imitation, a social-related process (perception/understanding of others and social communication). Participants are a healthy adult sample (n=37, ages 18–25). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation, group-level random-effects one-sample t-tests) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of activations; thus whole-brain healthy-group results are available. Although PPI connectivity is reported, they also provide univariate whole-brain activation maps for the imitation task and correlations with Urge. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

Although this paper reports an fMRI social-processing task (viewing/rating parents) with whole-brain, group-level univariate contrasts (mother vs. baseline; father vs. baseline) and clearly describes whole-brain results, the participant sample does not constitute a healthy adult group in the target age range. Participants are adolescents (mean age 17.0, range 15.47–18.72) and no separate analysis is reported for a healthy adult subgroup (age 17–65). Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample) is not met. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social task), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), I6 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately). No exclusion criteria from the list are strictly met; exclusion is based on failure to satisfy I4.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=33, ages 18–21) that used a task manipulating sociality (social vs non-social scenes) during task-based fMRI and reported group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (social > non-social; FDR corrected, p<0.05; Table 1 and Figure 1). The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion, and reports ROI analyses in addition to an explicitly described whole-brain activation map. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social reputation processing (a social-related task) conducted in healthy adult participants (N=28, ages 20–24). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (positive vs. neutral; negative vs. neutral) with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction and provides peak coordinates (Table 1 and figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete and adequate for screening.

This article reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind) using the EmpaToM paradigm in healthy adult samples (Experiments with N=25, 65, 178; ages reported within 17–65). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (emotionally negative > neutral; ToM > nonToM) with statistical thresholds and activation peak tables/coordinates, and describes random-effects analyses and resting-state connectivity. Behavioral and neural results for the healthy groups are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social gaze-following task with political in-group/out-group stimuli (social-related processing). Sample: 28 healthy adults aged 18–36, reported separately and meeting the age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (incongruent > congruent), thresholding, cluster correction, and tables/figures with reported coordinates, suitable as whole-brain activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text provided appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a validated social (Theory of Mind) task (moving-triangles animations), with a healthy adult sample (N=20; ages 24–64) within the 17–65 range. The authors report group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., ToM > R, ToM > Baseline) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level inference, and provide peak coordinates and figures. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical study). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain task activation maps, but the task is emotional picture viewing (negative/positive/neutral IAPS) focused on emotion processing rather than an explicit social-related task/construct. Although the authors discuss dmPFC (a region implicated in social cognition) and stimuli sometimes include people, the experimental manipulation targets negative emotion processing and not clearly a social construct such as affiliation, social communication, or perception/understanding of others. Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (none of E2–E6 are met). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates empathy for pain as modulated by experimentally induced (ingroup/outgroup) social categories — a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). The sample consists of 30 healthy adult participants (ages 18–35), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses (main effect of pain, main effect of condition, pain×condition interaction) with cluster-level and FWE-corrected results and tables described in the text, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are presented for the healthy/control group and are generalizable to healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, ages within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 23.6) that used task-based functional MRI while participants viewed social interactions (violent dyadic interactions) and manipulated attentional focus—this addresses social perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., all conditions vs baseline; focus on aggressor vs victim) with statistical maps, cluster correction, and coordinates/figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (fiction passages varying Social vs Non-social; relates to Theory of Mind), with a healthy adult sample (N=26, ages 19–26) and behavioral ToM measures. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., Social>Non-social and Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates (Table 1), satisfying whole-brain univariate reporting. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 17–65, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social-related processing. The task included implicit social stimuli (pictures depicting humans) and self-referential judgments; the sample comprised 28 healthy adults aged 30–50. The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses (ANOVA and direct contrasts/conjunctions) with results thresholded and reported (FDR-corrected; cluster extent) and described in text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is present and sufficient for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Cyberball social exclusion) with healthy adult participants (unmarried university students), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exclusion vs inclusion) with coordinates/tables and whole-brain interaction and two-sample whole-brain comparisons. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all relevant inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (racial in-group/out-group disgust perception) using a passive face-viewing task, which qualifies as social-related processing. Participants were healthy adults (n=26 after exclusions; mean age 21.2), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA; corrected whole-brain clusters, coordinates, tables, and figures) including the critical interaction contrast ((disgusted out-group–neutral out-group)–(disgusted in-group–neutral in-group)). Whole-brain results are described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (processing agentic vs. communal trait words) using a valence classification task. Participants were healthy adult university students (age range 18–25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8; conjunction and pairwise contrasts; AlphaSim-corrected results) with coordinates and figures/tables of activations/deactivations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This report is an empirical fMRI study of social-communicative processing (understanding Naming vs. Requesting speech acts). It used task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (n=18 analyzed; ages 18–41), meeting the age/sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise contrasts, FDR-corrected) and tables/figures of activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical hyperscanning fMRI study of face-to-face social interaction (mutual gaze and joint attention) in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~21–23). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task analyses (GLM/SPM) with voxelwise results and tables of coordinates and cluster-level statistics (FWE-corrected), including contrasts such as MG2–MG1 and JA-related activations. Behavioral–neural correlations and ROI checks are supplementary but whole-brain task maps are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (dynamic social gestures) in healthy adults using a task contrasting social vs nonsocial gestures. The methods report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FLAME, cluster correction) with reported coordinates and figures, and results are provided for the healthy participant group (N=20, mean age 21.4, range 16.9–25.7). Although one participant is reported as age 16.9 (just below 17), the sample is described and analyzed as a healthy young adult group and group-level whole-brain results are reported, so inclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=59–60, mean age ~20) that used a social task probing interpersonal trust/distrust (control-of-trust/distrust), satisfying the review focus on social-related processing. The manuscript presents whole-brain, group-level univariate task activation contrasts (e.g., trust>age, distrust>age, trust+distrust>age) with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of results and reports exploratory connectivity analyses; results are clearly reported for the healthy sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=26; mean age 28.7) using task-based paradigms probing social perception and cognition (face-viewing, person-judgment), satisfying the review objective. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects parametric analyses (e.g., Fig. S1, Table S4) mapping target popularity effects across the brain, and describes these whole-brain results in the text and supplemental tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. ROI analyses are present but whole-brain results are also reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This fMRI study directly investigates social cognition (empathic concern/compassion) using an active task with empathy-evoking film clips and contextual framing, satisfying the review objective. Sample: 26 healthy adult participants (age mean 30.3, range within 17–65) — meets the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., sad vs neutral context, multisensory > unisensory) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results presented in tables and figures, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Whole-brain results are described in text, tables, and figures (Supplementary tables referenced), so coordinate/table/figure reporting is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy-group task maps). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts. The task directly probes social communication/interaction (perceived live vs recorded speech). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=29, ages 18–27) with results reported for the healthy group. Whole-brain contrasts (Live > Social; Social > Standard) are reported, thresholded and cluster-corrected, with figures/tables and region coordinates; individual-subject mentalizing localizer and group-level maps are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about others’ mental states) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–27). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (searchlight MVPA results combined via one-sample t tests, network-level analyses, and parallel univariate whole-brain mapping with cluster correction; Tables S2/S3 and figures display whole-brain results), satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The task probes perception/understanding of others, and healthy adult group results are reported and generalizable. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary figures/tables are referenced. No exclusion criteria are met.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study of social learning about others’ generosity (social cognition), with healthy adult participants (final N=26, ages 19–37). It includes full methods, MRI acquisition/preprocessing, behavioral and whole-brain voxelwise group-level univariate analyses (conjunctions, contrasts, cluster-corrected maps, peak coordinates, and tables/figures) clearly reported for the healthy group. The content appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range samples, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is appropriate for inclusion.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From available text: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — live eye contact) is satisfied. However I4 (sample: healthy adult participants 17–65) is not verifiable from the provided content, and I5 (reporting a group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for healthy controls) is not reported in the abstract. Because core information needed to confirm key inclusion criteria is missing, the study is excluded pending a complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the available content.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an rt-fMRI+EEG neurofeedback study targeting social communication and right pSTS, satisfying I3 (fMRI during social-related task). However the provided content does not report participant sample details (cannot confirm healthy adults 17–65; I4 not met) nor present any group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation maps for a healthy group (I5 not met). Cannot determine whether results are ROI-only or include whole-brain maps. Because core article content (methods, participants, group whole-brain results) is missing, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is excluded pending full text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively applied from available info.

This is an fMRI study of affective theory-of-mind (social cognition) using a task manipulating emotional facial expressions during cartoon stories. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=21 analyzed; mean age ~23.7) within the 17–65 range. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-tests, whole-brain contrasts, tables of peak coordinates and figures) in the healthy sample, and also presents results in text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment probing social-related processing (effects of receiving cognitively and emotionally empathic comments) in healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 26). The paper provides whole-brain, group-level univariate activation results (voxelwise contrasts; FWE-corrected clusters and tables of activations are reported), not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and whole-brain analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment of social processing (perception of others’ facial expressions) in healthy adult participants (n=24, mean age 25.2), satisfying I3 and I4. The authors performed first-level and mixed-effects group-level univariate analyses (parameter estimate maps registered to MNI) and report a group-level faces>scrambled-faces localiser contrast used to define ROIs, which constitutes whole-brain, group-level task-evoked univariate results generalizable to healthy adults (I5). The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and the text describes whole-brain results (I6 acceptable). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, patient-only samples, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-evaluative task (watching positive, negative, neutral social videos) in a healthy adult sample (N=37, mean age 24.8). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate contrasts (positive>neutral, negative>neutral, conjunction) with family-wise error corrected results and cluster coordinates in tables and figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (race perception and trustworthiness evaluations) using a task involving face perception and trustworthiness ratings, satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants were 30 healthy right-handed White adults aged 18–29, meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate voxelwise analyses (e.g., Black>White contrast, second-level covariate analyses) with cluster-thresholding and tables of peak coordinates, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are presented in tables/figures and described in text (acceptable reporting per I6). Although the paper also reports PPI connectivity analyses, these supplement rather than replace whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This fMRI study investigates social cognition (linking person perception and person knowledge) using a task where participants view bodies or names paired with trait or neutral statements. It reports behavioral and group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (main effects and interaction contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds and tables of coordinates, and includes healthy adult participants (n=21, mean age 24.6). Whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts (e.g., Bodies>Names, Traits>Neutral, interaction) are clearly described and generalizable to healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind) using a task with social and non-social stories. Participants were healthy adults (N=24, mean age 25.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects univariate analyses (voxel-wise threshold P<0.001, cluster-wise FWE-corrected results shown in Tables 2–3) and ROI/MVPA analyses; whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy sample are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses fMRI during social-related tasks (social judgment of dominance and trustworthiness); (I4) sample comprises healthy adults aged 21–43 (n=23); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrast (Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment) with FWE-corrected cluster results and a table of coordinates; (I6) whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures and clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI examining social-related processing (meaning vs physical judgments of symbolic artifacts), uses a healthy adult sample (25 right-handed adults, mean age 24), and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise univariate results (random-effects SPM8 analyses with thresholding and tables/figures of activations and peak coordinates). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an fMRI study using the Cyberball (ball-toss) social interaction task (social reward/affiliation), conducted in healthy adult participants (final N=31; ages ~21). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task activation results with voxelwise coordinates and cluster-level inference (voxel p<0.005, cluster FWE p<0.05) for contrasts relevant to social interaction. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects generalizable to healthy adults. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This task-state fMRI study focuses on self-referential processing (a social-related construct), but it does not report a group-level univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation map for healthy adults. Instead, analyses are ROI-based and seed-based voxel-level functional connectivity (task-state connectivity) and between-group connectivity differences. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task fMRI addressing self-referential/social processing). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participant ages for healthy/control group are not provided to confirm they fall within 17–65), I5 (no group-level univariate whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group), I6 (not applicable because I5 not satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only seed-/connectivity-based analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (the paper emphasizes between-group connectivity differences and lacks an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI of a clearly social paradigm (socially-induced cognitive emotion regulation by a psychotherapist), using healthy adult participants (female, ages 22–32). Group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts are reported (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction, tables and coordinates, and behavioral correlations; methods, results and discussion are present in the full text. This meets inclusion for social-related fMRI task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective. It uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) addressing social-emotional processing (retaliation/provocation) (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=15; mean age 22.3), within the 17–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects group maps, Talairach coordinates, figures, and cluster-corrected thresholds) clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group (I5). Whole-brain results are provided in tables of coordinates and figures (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical study limitations). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Note: sample size is small and limited to young males, a limitation for generalizability but not an exclusion under the stated criteria.

The abstract and highlights indicate the study used fMRI during an interactive mentalizing (prisoner’s dilemma) paradigm—a social cognition task—and reports neural activation findings (bilateral temporal pole, precunei, right middle/superior frontal gyri) in a healthy adult sample (n=195 overall, fMRI subgroup n=163). These indicate group-level, task-evoked voxelwise results consistent with whole-brain univariate analyses typical for NeuroImage reports. Therefore the study appears to meet inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants), and I5 (whole-brain task-evoked results). However, the provided “full text” is incomplete (only highlights, abstract, and references are present), so I cannot fully verify that statistical maps are unmasked, clearly identified as healthy-group maps, or that all reporting conventions meet I5/I6. Due to that uncertainty I set fulltext_incomplete=true and a moderate confidence score.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (charitable giving, empathy, perspective taking) in healthy adults (N=33; ages 20–34).
