The paper reports task-based fMRI with whole-brain analyses: group-level GLMs and random-effects contrasts (e.g., EmpaToM contrasts used to define voxels, univariate GLM results reported including a significant visual-cortex cluster for low>high donations), and multiple whole-brain, voxelwise MVPA/SVR/searchlight results and group-level statistics. Results are reported as group-level maps/tables and described in the text and tables. Thus it meets inclusion I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported), and I6 (results presented in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Excluded because the study reports only functional connectivity / network analyses during task and rest and does not present any group-level univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (connectivity-only analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used fMRI with an emotion face matching task that falls under social perception/understanding of others) and I4 (healthy adult sample from the Human Connectome Project). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported group-level, univariate whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample (N=178, mean age 40.9 within 17–65). It uses a social cognition task (EmpaToM) manipulating empathy and Theory of Mind, and presents group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (emotional vs neutral videos; ToM vs non-ToM questions/videos) with statistical maps/coordinate tables and results generalizable to the healthy group. Methods, results, and discussion are fully reported in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only highlights, abstract, abbreviations, keywords, and references provided). Inclusion I3 (fMRI during a social task: cooperation vs. competition) is met based on the abstract. However, I4 (explicit sample details confirming healthy adult participants aged 17–65) is not verifiable from the provided content. I5 (reporting of at least one group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group) cannot be confirmed — the abstract mentions univariate analyses but does not provide or state whole-brain group-level maps or coordinate tables. I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement) also cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the available text. Because core methods/results and participant details are missing, I must exclude pending a complete full text.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI social-learning task (I3 met). However the report does not provide participant demographics or specify that the sample consists of healthy adults aged 17–65 (I4 not verifiable) and does not provide the full methods/results needed to confirm that at least one group-level, univariate whole-brain task activation map for the healthy group is reported (I5 not verifiable). Because the full text (methods and results) is unavailable, I cannot confirm compliance with I4 and I5 required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be positively identified from the abstract alone. Recommend obtaining the full text to reassess inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of social impression updating (a social cognitive task involving perception/understanding of others), with a healthy adult sample (N=21, ages 18–31). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (e.g., L2>F3 contrasts, 2×4 ANOVA, corrected thresholds using AlphaSim) with tables/figures of activations and extracted parameter estimates. Results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses, and healthy-group whole-brain effects are clearly reported and generalizable to adults in the target age range. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of Theory of Mind (REMICS task) directly probing social cognition/mentalizing. Participants: 19 healthy adults age 20–53 (within 17–65). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level correction, and provides tables of activation coordinates and figures. Thus it provides univariate whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps generalizable to healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, out-of-range ages) apply. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and tables/figures, so fulltext is complete.

This is an original fMRI study of social processing (modified Cyberball task combining social exclusion and performance evaluation) in healthy adults (n=40, mean age 27.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Exclusion > Inclusion; PG EX > FG EX), using FWE correction and provides tables of peak coordinates and conjunction analyses, which are clearly described. Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (naturalistic movie viewing) in healthy adults (N=34, mean age 22.2), and uses functional MRI during a social-related task (meets I3). The sample is within the 17–65 range and reported for a healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise reverse-correlation analyses and presents group-level whole-brain maps/clusters (e.g., Fig. 3) and statistical tests, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not out-of-age-range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (observation of others acting in angry vs. joyful contexts), with a healthy adult sample (20 participants, ages 23–33). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., angry session > joyful session; AG > joyful grasping) with cluster- and voxel-level FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-task fMRI), I4 (healthy adults within 17–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level univariate task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This article meets all inclusion criteria: I3 – task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self-reference vs other-reference); I4 – healthy adult sample reported (n=110, ages 19–31); I5 – group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked maps/contrasts are reported (SR>OR, OR>SR, SR+OR>baseline) with appropriate statistical thresholds; I6 – whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical work. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports task-based fMRI in social contexts (economic games with manipulated sociality: Prisoner’s Dilemma, Ultimatum/Welfare Game), meeting the review objective. Participant samples are healthy adults (college-aged; Pilot N=10, Main N=15) with methods and results reported separately for the healthy groups. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain, univariate analyses (first-/second-/third-level GLM in FSL/FLAME and SPM12) and reports thresholded activation maps and coordinate tables (e.g., contrasts shown at P<0.05 FWE), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Although PPI connectivity is also reported, whole-brain task activation maps are present (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only), and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social/attachment-related task (AAP attachment vs matched neutral scenes) in healthy adults (N=25, age range 19–26). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (attachment vs neutral; cluster-level corrected results with MNI coordinates and t-values) and provides coordinates and figures of the activations (e.g., IPL/TPJ, MTG, mPFC). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the 17–65 range). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The full text reports an fMRI study of social cognition (cooperation/competition; self vs other processing) in healthy adult participants (final N=24, ages 19–31). The task is social-related and uses task-based functional MRI (I3). The healthy adult sample is within 17–65 and results for that group are reported separately (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation results (family-wise error cluster-corrected maps, peak coordinates in Table 1 and whole-brain figures; generalizable healthy-group effects) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I5,I6). The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplemental references) is present, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range samples) apply.

This fMRI study used a social task (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) probing cooperation and social reward, satisfying I3. Participants were healthy adults (female university students; final imaging N=18; mean age ~21), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., CC vs. other outcomes; context×cooperation interactions) with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates in tables, satisfying I5 and I6. ROI analyses are present but are supplemented by univariate whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment using a social-related task (Social Detection Task) probing perception/understanding of others and mental state attribution. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=38, ages 18–30) and results for the healthy group are reported separately. The manuscript reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain univariate analyses (first- and second-level GLMs, a full-factorial ANOVA) and whole-brain contrasts (e.g., Social > Non-social) with FWE cluster correction and tabulated activations/coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of emotion regulation (reappraisal) in response to angry faces, a social stimulus relevant to social perception/understanding. The sample comprises healthy adults (N=60; age range 18–57) with resting-state subset N=48, meeting the adult age and healthy-group requirements. The manuscript presents multiple group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry; Increase vs Observe-angry; Increase+Decrease vs Observe-angry) with coordinates, cluster thresholds and tables, clearly identified as healthy-group effects and thresholded with FWE cluster correction. Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables (supplementary material available). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=31 males, age 19–32) that investigates prosocial learning using a task-based functional MRI paradigm (meets I3 and I4). The paper reports group-level, univariate task-evoked analyses with whole-brain analysis procedures described (main effects reported at P < 0.05 FWE whole-brain or SVC; figures and tables of activations and supplementary tables are provided), satisfying the requirement for a group-level, voxelwise healthy-control task map reported in the text/figures/tables (meets I5 and I6). The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy adult results, and is an original empirical report. Full text provided (introduction, methods, results, discussion); fulltext_incomplete set to false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial behavior) in healthy adult participants (N=32 healthy females, mean age 22.7), and reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts (e.g., Mentalizing > baseline; Dissimilar > Similar) with cluster-level inference and coordinate tables. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about friends vs kin) using a task performed in the scanner, meeting the review objective. Participants: 25 healthy adult females (mean age 23.2), within the 17–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked analyses (friend > kin contrast and parametric linear analyses across network layers) with cluster-corrected results, tables of coordinates, and figures—all clearly described for the healthy participant group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts without healthy-group task effects, out-of-range ages, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in a social/emotion paradigm (Face Matching Task with fearful and neutral faces), includes a healthy adult sample (n=10, mean age 25 within 17–65), and provides group-level univariate whole-brain GLM results (one-sample t-tests; contrasts reported, with figures/tables in main/supplementary material). Whole-brain maps/coordinate tables are described and available in supplementary files, satisfying acceptability per I6. Although the paper also reports ICA connectivity analyses, it additionally reports univariate whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group, so no exclusion criteria (E2–E4) are triggered. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, conclusions).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (competitive social context) in healthy adults (20 right-handed females, age 18–35). The task explicitly manipulates social competition (social comparison/mentalizing) during a working-memory/feedback paradigm and uses fMRI. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM), corrected cluster thresholds, contrasts (e.g., Competition > No Competition), and peak coordinates; results are reported for the healthy participant group. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining social communication: participants viewed product descriptions varying in social-language and fMRI was recorded during a task about recommending products. Sample: healthy adult undergraduates (n=19; mean age 20.55), within 17–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (parametric modulators, whole-brain maps, thresholding and corrected results) and presents tables/figures of whole-brain activations associated with social language in and social language out. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related processing in healthy adults, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (emotion recognition and gaze integration), meeting the social-related task requirement (I3). It includes a healthy younger adult group aged 17–27, satisfying the sample requirement (I4); although an older group (65–75) is also included, results are reported separately by age group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task analyses (PLS-based whole-brain patterns) with tables of peak coordinates, cluster information, figures, and brain-behavior correlations, providing whole-brain, generalizable healthy-group results (I5,I6). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age-out-of-range-only participants, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

While this is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (I3 and I4 satisfied), the full text reports whole-brain analyses only in the form of between-group contrasts (STRESS > CONTROL and BIOPSY > QTIP etc.) and conjunctions of these between-group contrasts. I find no clear, unmasked, group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported specifically for a healthy/control group (e.g., INJECTION > QTIP within the control group or a main effect across the healthy sample) that would meet inclusion criterion I5. Therefore the study effectively reports only between-group whole-brain contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect, matching exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related empathy-for-pain task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain healthy-group task map). Exclusion applied: E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (emotion attribution/perception of others) in healthy adult participants. The sample consists of healthy adults within the 17–65 age range (N=18 recruited; analyses on 16–17 participants; ages 21–46). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (Explicit Task Emotion>Expression conjunctions, Implicit Task Face>Scramble contrasts) with cluster-level correction and whole-brain statistical maps described and displayed; ROI analyses are also reported but whole-brain results are clearly present. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references) is provided in the submission. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only, age within range, and is empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (perception of emotional facial expressions, including affiliation-relevant emotions), using 40 healthy volunteers and examines associations with extraversion. The abstract reports voxelwise brain activation in multiple regions (thalamus, temporo-parietal regions, cerebellum, amygdala, cortical areas), indicating whole-brain, group-level univariate task effects generalizable to healthy adults. Thus inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked results), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats) are met. However, the provided content appears to be truncated (only highlights/abstract/metadata present) and lacks full methods and results sections, so fulltext_incomplete is true; this lowers confidence. Recommend obtaining the complete full text to confirm participant ages and analytic details.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (face emotion/age judgments) in healthy adults (n=25, ages 21–33). The task probes perception/understanding of others (emotion), satisfying I3. The sample is within the 17–65 range and healthy, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate analyses (random-effects GLM for faces > objects localizer and second-level whole-brain searchlight analyses), satisfying I5 and reported in-text and figures/tables (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only analyses, no connectivity/resting-only focus, and healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (recognition of social interactions from point-light displays) and includes a clearly defined healthy adult group (n=16; ages 20–41). The study reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts (SI > NM) analyzed with SPM8 and presents voxelwise results and cluster/FWE-corrected activations for the adult group (figures/tables described). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level univariate task maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This empirical fMRI study of healthy adults (n=41 and n=39; ages 18–24) examines social-related processing (self-related and social/mentalizing constructs) during an article-reading task and links neural activity to population-level sharing. The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain searches; Fig. S3 and Table S5) in addition to ROI analyses. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (retrieval of person/biographical knowledge), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=24 and n=26; mean ages within 17–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., “all memory conditions > baseline”, status memory > baseline, trait memory > baseline; voxel-level FWE-corrected maps and tables of coordinates are provided), along with MVPA, PPI, and DCM. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate maps), and I6 (results described and reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI experiment using a social cognition (mentalising/theory-of-mind) task (I3). Participants are healthy adults within the target age range (Experiment 2: mean age 22, N=17; Experiment 1: N=39, mean age 35.5) meeting the sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts (mentalising > factual; parametric modulation) analyzed in SPM with thresholding and tables/figures of significant activations and coordinates (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is INCLUDED.

This fMRI study assesses social processing (Cyberball exclusion), so it meets I3. However, the sample consists of adolescent males (16–17 years) rather than a clear healthy adult group (I4 not met). Crucially, the manuscript reports task-based functional connectivity results (within-network and whole-brain parcellation connectivity) but does not present any group-level univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables from the healthy/control group in the provided full text or supplemental description; therefore it does not satisfy I5/I6. This means the study effectively reports only connectivity analyses without accompanying healthy-group whole-brain activation maps, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete for the main article (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given these violations, the study must be excluded from the review.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (pseudo-interactive joke task assessing action-outcome contingency and self/other processing). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=38, ages 19–29) with analyses reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts (e.g., SELF minus OTHER; Listener’s response contrasts; interaction/action-outcome contingency) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction; results include tables of peak coordinates and figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not between-group-only; ages within range; empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study examining social-related processing (decisions to share/select news articles) in healthy adults (N=41 after exclusions; ages 18–24), meeting the review’s domain and sample requirements. The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (select > content, share > content, share > select) and describes whole-brain analyses with family-wise error correction and corresponding tables/figures (Tables 2, 4; Figs. 4, 5), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task effects. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy group only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This article reports an fMRI study of social decision-making in healthy adult participants (neuroimaging cohort ages 18–57, n=62 after exclusions). The task explicitly manipulates social information (Locations, Points, Both, Isolated) and uses whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (GLM, random effects, voxelwise maps thresholded and corrected; maps deposited on NeuroVault). Methods and results include whole-brain statistical maps and parametric regressors tied to social versus non-social inputs. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–57 within 17–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps generalizable to healthy adults), and I6 (whole-brain results presented and described; NeuroVault link). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making (Trust Game) meeting the review objective. It uses task-based fMRI during a clearly social reciprocity task, includes a healthy adult sample (ages 18–30; n=19 included in imaging analyses), and reports group-level univariate whole-brain task-evoked results (contrasts, voxelwise thresholds, cluster-correction, tables/figures of activations). Whole-brain results are described in text, tables and figures. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and this is an empirical study).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used task-based fMRI during a social cognition paradigm (mental simulation of personally familiar others), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=23 after exclusions; ages 18–27), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results (searchlight MVPA and random-effects t tests producing whole-brain statistical maps, cluster tables with peak voxels and corrections for multiple comparisons), satisfying I5 and reporting coordinates/tables per I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs, connectivity-only analyses, non-adult samples, or non-empirical data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study examines social-emotional processing (schadenfreude and fremdscham) using a task involving observation of others' social integrity threats, meeting the review objective. Sample: N=34 healthy adult participants (ages 19–31) reported separately for the healthy/control group. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (SIT vs NEUT) with FWE-corrected results and tables/figures, and explicitly describes whole-brain analyses and results; whole-brain findings are also described in text. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind/implicit belief processing) in healthy adult participants (mean age 24.4, N=22 analyzed). The paper reports a whole-brain random-effects GLM from the explicit general-belief localizer (false-belief vs false-photograph) with thresholded group-level results and Talairach coordinates, satisfying the requirement for a group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked map. The main implicit ToM task used an ROI approach but the explicit localizer provides whole-brain evidence. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets I3 (uses task-based fMRI during social cognition/theory-of-mind tasks) and I4 (healthy adult samples, ages within 17–65). However, the full text presents ROI-based MVPA results and individualized ROI definitions (ToM localizer at the subject level) and does not report any group-level, univariate whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group that is generalizable to healthy adults. No group-level whole-brain activation maps or coordinate tables of such univariate contrasts are clearly described in the provided text (figures/supplement referenced but no explicit group-level univariate map reported). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate results) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based BOLD responses to socially relevant stimuli (romantic and sexual images), addressing affiliation/attachment constructs. Sample comprises 20 healthy adult men aged 22–50, reported separately (monogamous vs non-monogamous groups). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked statistical analyses (random-effects FLAME, cluster correction) and presents whole-brain contrasts and figures/tables (sexual>neutral; romantic>neutral; within-group contrasts). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigated implicit attitudes and executive control in romantically involved adult males using task-based fMRI (IAT with monogamy/adultery stimuli and a go/no-go inhibition task with attractive female faces). The tasks probe social/affiliation and attachment-related processing. The sample comprised healthy adults aged 20–32 (right-handed, no neurological/psychiatric history). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (IAT incongruent vs. congruent) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/coordinates, and also reports task-related activation results for the go/no-go contrast (with targeted VLPFC results). Thus the paper provides whole-brain task-evoked maps for a healthy adult group and meets the review’s reporting requirements. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). No exclusion criteria from the review were met.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social processing: subjects (N=14, ages 20–32) viewed stimuli depicting social interactions while BOLD data were acquired. It tests perception/understanding of others (social interactions), satisfying the social-related task criterion. The sample consists of healthy adults within the 17–65 range and is reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects group analyses (surface-based), including univariate, voxelwise contrasts (interaction > independent; animate > physical), and these group-level maps and results are described in the text and figures (and supplementary figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (impression-formation of others varying in race and SES), satisfying the meta-analysis domain. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8) within the 17–65 range. The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain regressions with voxelwise thresholding and reported significant clusters, e.g., VMPFC), meeting the whole-brain result requirement; acceptable reporting formats (figures/tables/supplement) are used. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group map, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=16, mean age 22.75) during a social-related task (perception/interpretation of body motion and potential for social involvement). The methods describe whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (GLM) with contrasts reported and stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1), voxelwise results thresholded and described for mirror-neuron and mentalizing networks, satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete for screening. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate task results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

Exclusion(s) met: E3. Inclusion(s) met: I3, I4. Inclusion(s) not met: I5. Rationale: The study examines attachment-related social processing using fMRI in healthy adult participants (behavioral N=149; fMRI sample N=23 males), satisfying I3 (social/attachment construct) and I4 (healthy adults 17–65). However, the neuroimaging results reported are seed-based, resting-state functional connectivity analyses (post-narrative FC of caudate nucleus) rather than group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the healthy group. The paper does not present an univariate whole-brain task activation map or within-group task contrast generalizable to healthy adults, so it fails I5 and meets exclusion E3. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/collaborative learning in healthy adult participants (ages reported within 18–33). The task is social/communicative (collaborative referential communication) and the paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Collaborative > Individual, Individual > Arbitrary) with cluster correction and tables/figures. Whole-brain results are described and an ROI analysis is supplementary, not replacing whole-brain reporting. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction processing in healthy adults (N=36, ages ~24–25), using task-based fMRI with whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (categorical and parametric contrasts reported; cluster-level FDR corrections; Tables/Figures with coordinates). The paper additionally reports DCM connectivity analyses, but these are accompanied by whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates. All required inclusion criteria are met (task fMRI of social processing; healthy adult sample in age range; whole-brain group-level univariate results reported and clearly described). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (joint action/haptic coordination) in healthy adult participants (ages within 17–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts with Talairach coordinates and corrected thresholds (FDR), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The task probes social-cognitive constructs (leading, following, mutuality; mentalizing, social reward), fulfilling the social-related task criterion. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used task-based fMRI while participants listened to affective vocalisations (a social communication/perception task), included a healthy adult sample (N=19, ages within 17–65), and reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., species contrast human>chimpanzee>macaque) with MNI coordinates and statistics. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the report appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

The study includes a social cognition task (TOM vs Random) using task-based fMRI in a large sample of healthy adults from the Human Connectome Project (n=787), satisfying the social-related task construct. Participants are healthy adults within the 17–65 age range. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task activation maps (Cohen's d and level-3 z maps) derived from the healthy sample and presents whole-brain voxelwise results in figures and tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are clearly described and generalizable to healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social role judgment task (self, friend, celebrity) that probes perception/understanding of self and others (social-related processing). Sample: 37 healthy adult males (mean age 22.9), which falls within the 17–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (self vs. celebrity; friend vs. celebrity) with voxelwise statistics and FDR correction, and provides peak coordinates and tables/figures. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete.

The full text describes an fMRI study using an iterated prisoner's dilemma social decision-making task (meets I3). Sample: 20 healthy adult participants aged 23–38, reported as healthy and screened (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., conjunction of task>control, COMP>COOP) with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates, and extracts percent-signal-change from significant clusters (meets I5 and I6). The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods (behavioral and fMRI acquisition/preprocessing/GLM), Results (behavioral, whole-brain, time-course, gPPI), and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within the 17–65 range, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Therefore INCLUDE for the review of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study reports an empirical task-based fMRI experiment directly comparing social vs. non-social stimuli with healthy adult participants (ages 23–50) and uses whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses. Methods and results include a group-level social > non-social contrast with voxelwise thresholds and FDR correction, tables/figures of cluster results, and ROI/whole-brain conjunction analyses. The sample is healthy adults (n=14 analyzed), and whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (group contrasts) are clearly reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related emotion perception task (perception/understanding of others via facial and prosodic cues), with healthy adult participants within the 17–65 range. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA and paired t-tests) with PFWE-corrected results, cluster tables and coordinates, and ROI analyses. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

Full text unavailable/incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). Inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is satisfied based on the abstract. However, critical inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed: I4 (participant ages 17–65 not reported in abstract), I5 (no clear report of a group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map in the provided content), and I6 (cannot verify acceptable whole-brain reporting). No exclusion criteria can be confidently applied from the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify whole-brain results or participant ages; therefore the study must be excluded at this stage pending full-text availability.

Only the abstract is provided (full text incomplete). The abstract indicates an fMRI study of social communicative intentions, satisfying I3 (social-related fMRI task). However the full text is not available to confirm critical eligibility requirements: participant characteristics (age range and health status) to satisfy I4 and whether group-level, univariate whole-brain voxelwise task maps are reported to satisfy I5/I6. Because I4 and I5 (and by extension I6) cannot be verified from the abstract alone, the study cannot be confirmed eligible and is excluded pending access to the complete article. No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 are clearly met based on the abstract.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluations) using a task-based design in healthy adults. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=31, ages 19–24). The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts and a whole-brain multiple regression with self-esteem as regressor, with results reported in tables of coordinates and thresholded maps (voxel-wise p<0.001, cluster-level FWE-corrected p<0.05). Psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analyses are additional connectivity analyses but do not replace the whole-brain task activations. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social evaluation in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4), but the analyses were restricted to predefined ROIs (search regions restricted to amygdala, insula, IFG, ACC, thalamus, caudate, mOFC) and no unmasked whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Includes an explicit social cognition task (social interaction vs. random movement) using task fMRI; participants are healthy adults drawn from HCP and UCLA datasets with ages within 21–50 (within 17–65 range); the paper reports group-level, voxel-wise task activation analyses and displays activation maps (e.g., Figure 1 and Supplementary figures) derived from healthy/control participants, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The study is empirical and not limited to ROI/connectivity-only outcomes. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Exclusion applied: E5 — the study sample consists of adolescents (ages 14–18, M=16.3) and does not report a separate healthy adult subgroup (17–65). Inclusion criteria met: I3 — the study uses task-based fMRI of a social-related task (social-reward/peer feedback); I6 — whole-brain results are reported in text/figures/tables (group-level contrasts are presented). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — no healthy adult participant group (17–65) is analyzed/reported separately; I5 — although group-level whole-brain maps are reported, they are from an adolescent sample and are not clearly generalizable to a healthy adult population. Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false. Because the review seeks fMRI evidence generalizable to healthy adults and this study reports only an adolescent healthy sample without an adult subgroup, it must be excluded under E5.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=55, mean age 24.9) using a social-related task (extended Hariri face/scene matching with erotic and fearful social scenes), satisfying the review objective. The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (e.g., erotic>neutral, fearful>neutral, erotic>fearful) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and ROI analyses; figures and tables of results are presented. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age out-of-range, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=22, mean age 24.4) that uses task-based fMRI during social-cognitive tasks (mind perception and gaze cueing). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (parametric regressors, FLAME1), cluster-level corrected results and coordinates (tables/figures) identifying vmPFC and other regions; results are described as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables. The sample falls within the 17–65 age range and results for the healthy group are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines maternal neural responses to their own child’s facial emotions (a social/attachment-related task), meeting the social-processing domain. It includes a healthy adult control group (mothers without early-life maltreatment) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task activation results (e.g., familiarity own>unknown in CON: medial frontal gyrus, pFWE<0.001) as well as other whole-brain and ROI analyses, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Confidence is high given clear within-group whole-brain reporting for the healthy control group.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI task explicitly probing social-related processing (recall of self- and other-relationship episodes), includes a healthy adult sample (n=35; diagnostic interview confirmed no mental disorders), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self-relevant>control, other>control) with FDR correction and clusterwise inference. Results are reported in tables and figures and are generalizable to a healthy adult group. The manuscript contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections, so the full text is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is unavailable (404 page on journal site). Based on title and metadata this may be an fMRI study of social interactions, but the core article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is not accessible, so key eligibility elements cannot be verified. Therefore I cannot confirm that the study: (I3) used fMRI during a social-related task; (I4) included a healthy adult group aged 17–65; (I5) reported a group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group; or (I6) provided whole-brain results in text/figures/tables. No exclusion criteria can be confidently applied from the available information. Full text incomplete prevents reliable inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions), conducted in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (random-effects, FWE-corrected maps and coordinates) demonstrating bimodal > unimodal effects (rpSTS) and congruency effects; results and statistical thresholds are described and tables/coordinates provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables described). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses fMRI during a social cognition task (face-based trustworthiness judgments with feedback), satisfying I3. It reports a healthy younger adult group (ages 20–33), satisfying I4 (healthy adults 17–65 present and reported separately). The paper presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (ANOVA and whole-brain results, with reported clusters and a Supplementary Table 2), satisfying I5; statistical thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction are described. Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures (coordinates and cluster peaks), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes an analysable healthy adult group within 17–65, and is empirical with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion included).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition that meets all inclusion criteria. It used task-based fMRI while participants made judgments about others’ mental states (social-related task), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adults (N=28 after one exclusion; ages 18–22), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses: a searchlight representational similarity analysis and voxelwise univariate repetition suppression analyses with permutation TFCE correction, reporting peak coordinates and clusters (medial PFC, posterior precuneus), satisfying I5 and I6 (results presented as corrected maps and coordinates/figures). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (a social decision-making task) performed during functional MRI, with analyses and results reported for a healthy adult sample. Sample: 20 healthy male adults (age range 21–37), meeting the healthy adult criterion. Whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses are reported (one-sample t tests, flexible factorial analyses; FWE cluster-corrected maps and tables of cluster activations are presented). Results are described in text, tables, and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the article meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n≈300 randomized; final analytic samples reported) using a social-interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) performed during BOLD fMRI, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–22 (within 17–65). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (thresholding, cluster correction, whole-brain results and coordinates described in text and tables; analyses reported for healthy/placebo and treatment groups and subgroup analyses), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain healthy maps, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult males (ages 18–35) using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes social processing (provocation, decision-making about another person). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts (high vs low provocation) with FWEc cluster correction and provides MNI coordinates and figures for these contrasts, clearly attributable to the healthy participant sample. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level univariate task maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not exclusively between-group contrasts, and participants are within the age range). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based dual-fMRI hyperscanning during an interactive social task (cooperation/competition, social exchange); (I4) healthy adult sample (N=44, mean age 22.37, ages within 17–65); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked analyses (GLM, FLAME random-effects, non-parametric permutation correction) with tables/figures of voxelwise results; (I6) whole-brain results are reported as tables of coordinates and whole-brain t-maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Full text unavailable (only abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract: the study uses fMRI during a social-related pleasant touch paradigm (I3) and includes a matched healthy control group (I4). However, the abstract does not provide sufficient information to confirm that at least one group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported (I5). Because the full text (methods/results) is not available, I cannot verify whole-brain results required by I5. Therefore the study is excluded pending full-text confirmation. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are definitively met based on available information.

Full text is incomplete: only journal metadata/title/abstract-like header provided. Cannot verify whether the study (1) used a social-related fMRI task reported for a healthy adult group (I3,I4), (2) reported at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map for the healthy/control group (I5,I6). Title suggests a study of young adult males with autism and resting state/overt interaction, but the available content does not allow confirmation of a healthy control group or presence of whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 can be confidently applied from the incomplete content. Therefore excluded due to incomplete/full-text unavailability preventing verification of required inclusion criteria.

Full text available here is limited to title/abstract/metadata; core methods/results not accessible. Abstract confirms task-based fMRI of a social cognition construct (theory of mind) — meets I3. However, participant ages are not specified in the abstract so I4 (healthy adult group aged 17–65) cannot be confirmed. The abstract describes resting-state intrinsic connectivity and task-defined networks but does not clearly report a group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (I5 not verifiable). Because essential inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study is excluded pending full-text access. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively applied based on the available information.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses fMRI during a social-related task: dynamic facial expression localizer). Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be verified from provided content: I4 (no explicit information confirming a healthy adult group aged 17–65 and separate reporting), I5 (no explicit whole-brain, group-level univariate task-evoked statistical map shown or described in the provided content), I6 (unclear whether whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables/supplements). Exclusion criteria met: none (no evidence in provided content that E2–E6 apply). Because core methods/results needed to confirm I4 and I5 are missing, I exclude this record pending access to the complete full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (face perception/recognition — ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’), with healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: N=20, mean age ~25; additional behavioral samples also healthy). The paper reports group-level fMRI analyses including a group-level univariate localizer contrast (faces vs scrambled; n=83) used to define ROIs and describes mixed-effects (FLAME) group analyses registered to MNI space, satisfying the requirement for a group-level, task-evoked whole-brain map generalizable to healthy adults. Results and methods are fully reported (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so full text appears complete. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: I3 — it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (live bidirectional conversation contrasting human–human and human–robot interactions, addressing social communication/mentalizing/social motivation); I4 — includes a healthy adult sample (n=21 after exclusions; mean age 25.8, within 17–65); I5 — reports group-level, whole-brain univariate voxelwise task contrasts (HHI vs HRI) analyzed with SPM and thresholded at p<0.05 FDR cluster-level, with figures and NeuroVault/OpenNeuro data shared; I6 — whole-brain results are clearly described in text and figures (and shared online). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not restricted to non-healthy or out-of-range ages, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (empathy toward human vs robot), using healthy adult participants (n=26, ages 18–27). It includes group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-corrected and uncorrected maps), reports whole-brain results in text/figures/tables, and shares maps on NeuroVault/OSF. The full article (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study reports task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample (n=20, ages 22–35) using a social-communication paradigm (naturalistic narrative with co-speech gestures). The paper provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., low_ID > high_ID; speech > gestures+speech; gestures+speech > speech) with tables of activation peaks, cluster extents, and thresholding procedures, clearly attributable to the healthy participant group. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is available. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are within 17–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the review.

This study uses fMRI with a social task (cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group, so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met. However, the full text reports primarily between-group contrasts (BPD vs NSSI, conjunctions vs HC) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map specifically for the healthy control group (no HC within-group whole-brain task effect is reported). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map).

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (animacy perception/perception of others); (I4) samples healthy adult participants (ages reported 19–36, healthy, N=111 overall, N≈36 included in fMRI analyses); (I5) reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (whole-brain conjunctions and FWE-corrected voxelwise results, reported in figures and tables); (I6) whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: it includes multiple social cognition tasks (false belief, animacy/intentional triangles, eyes intention, trustworthiness, face and vocalization tasks) that probe perception/understanding of others. Sample: 78 healthy adults (age 18–40), meeting the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (RFX) with maps thresholded at p<0.05 FWE and provides Tables/figures of whole-brain results and NeuroVault availability; thus it provides univariate whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets inclusion criteria: I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing—observation of dynamic facial expressions, a social communication/perception task), I4 (healthy adult sample: n=51, ages within 17–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain univariate analyses—random-effects one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs with voxel-wise family-wise error correction), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text, with tables/figures and coordinates). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state only; includes healthy-group whole-brain task activations).

This study should be excluded because it does not report any group-level, univariate whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps for the healthy adult group. Instead, the paper presents ROI-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical analyses using the Power-264 atlas. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: vocal emotional processing/social communication) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 20–35). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (reports only ROI/atlas-based connectivity analyses with no whole-brain results) and E3 (reports connectivity/graph-theory analyses without accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports an fMRI study using social tasks (take-advice game and trust game) clearly probing social cognition/trust (meets I3). Sample comprises 31 healthy adult participants (age mean 24.3), meeting I4. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain univariate results (voxel- and cluster-level FWE thresholds, contrasts such as honesty>dishonesty, value contrasts, and Supplementary Tables with coordinates), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, task, imaging acquisition/preprocessing, GLMs), Results, Discussion, and References, so core content is present and complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, no between-group-only contrasts, and participants are within age range). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study uses task-based fast fMRI to compare vocal (socially relevant) versus non-vocal sounds, addressing social communication/perception of others (I3). Participants are healthy adults within the 17–65 range (Experiment 1: n=13, mean age ~26.6; Experiment 2: n=18, mean age ~23.1), satisfying sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation contrasts (vocal > non-vocal) with thresholding and coordinates/figures (Fig.1 and described GLM results), providing whole-brain univariate task-evoked maps generalizable to healthy adults (I5/I6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; not truncated. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., this is not ROI-only, not resting-state only, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This paper reports task-based functional MRI during observation of social (interpersonal) touch scenes (MVPA and univariate analyses) and thus addresses social-related processing. The sample includes a clearly reported healthy neurotypical adult control group (n=21) analyzed separately from the ASD group. The manuscript reports group-level univariate whole-brain task contrasts and provides mean group effects and coordinate tables/figures (see Additional file 1, Figure S2 and Table S2) for the healthy/control group. Results are presented as voxelwise contrasts and are generalizable to healthy adults. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary results) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy task maps, participants are adults, and this is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 22–39) investigating how collective/social schemas influence memory; the paradigm and analyses probe social-related constructs (collective memory, social knowledge, mentalizing-related dmPFC responses). The sample meets the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain searchlight results (TFCE-corrected maps; Extended Data Fig.1) derived from regressions of representational similarity metrics, which constitute group-level voxelwise statistical maps generalizable to the healthy group. Results are reported in the main text and extended figures/tables. The study is empirical and includes full methods, results, and discussion, and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical approaches. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.
